title: Xpeng Says It Can Quickly Adapt Car Autopilot Systems for Europe
summary: Xpeng Inc. can rapidly adapt its advanced driver-assistance technology to European roads using relatively small amounts of data, allowing it to modify its software capabilities for different markets without rebuilding them from scratch.

title: Is AI Crowding Everyone Else Out of the Bond Market?
summary: Hyperscalers, data centers and chip companies are borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars to finance the AI buildout, turning the technology boom into one of the biggest new forces in corporate credit. Investors are still buying, but rising concentration, complex data-center financing and competition with government borrowing are raising a harder question: how much AI debt can the market absorb? (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Smart Home Launch Oct. 13 Plans; HomeView Has Mid-November Release
summary: Fresh details on Apple’s HomeView, HomePod mini and new Apple TV, including release dates, colors, chips and features.

title: Apple Supplier Luxshare Expects No Material Impact From US Probe
summary: Apple Inc. supplier Luxshare Precision Industry Co. is facing a US patent investigation into data-center power technologies following infringement allegations by Vicor Corp., according to a filing on Saturday.

title: Nvidia Explores Deal Options With Reflection AI, Financial Times Says
summary: Nvidia Corp. is in talks to boost its investment in Reflection AI or offer the startup computing power, a move that would strengthen ties with a key developer of open-weight models, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Microsoft CEO Nadella Calls for ‘Emergency Brake’ on Advanced AI
summary: Microsoft Corp. Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said companies should treat powerful artificial intelligence models as potential insider threats, assume they could be compromised and create an “emergency brake” system to prevent agentic models from going rogue.
